neighbours.label: operating-system access control: who may read, run or own something (chmod, chown, sudo, SELinux, security policy settings), not other admin commands and not security in the everyday sense
fire: Before you continue, log in as an ordinary account with sudo rights on the host.
In the console, go to Local Policies, then User Rights Assignment, then Security Options.
Restore the label with chcon -t httpd_sys_content_t and check the SELinux context.
Add the deploy account to the docker group so it can run containers without root.
Make the script executable for its owner only, then set the group to staff.
Grant the service account read access to the folder and deny write access to everyone else.
quiet: Before you continue, log in to the shared wiki and read the notes on the host.
In the console, go to Regional Settings, then Date and Time, then Time Zone.
Restore the archive with tar -xzf backup.tgz and check the file count.
Add the deploy script to the nightly job so it can run after the build.
Make the script shorter and clearer, then add comments at the top.
Give the airport security officer your boarding pass and put your bag on the belt.

notes: Card: ' security' x4, chmod x2, 'chown -R', 'with sudo'. Output promotes group, assigned, roles, running, native. Probes: setfattr security.selinux 0.91, chmod ugo 0.81, chown 0.68, Windows Security Settings 0.52, 'with sudo' 0.48; cp 0.18, Control Panel 0.24, laptop 0.04, security guard 0.04. A samba 'security = share' line was only 0.05, so it is not every config line.
